newsitem.title: ITALY: Symbolism abounds as Bossi sets out across Italy.
newsitem.headline: Symbolism abounds as Bossi sets out across Italy.

text.p: Umberto Bossi's three-day trek across northern Italy from the mountains in the west to the sea in the east to declare "independence" for "Padania" is a truly symbolic journey.

At the heart of the separatist Northern League leader's travels to a promised declaration in the lagoon city of Venice on Sunday lies the river Po, bisecting Italy and the region he dreams of transforming into a separate republic.

On Friday, in a grand opening gesture laden with quasi-religious symbolism, Bossi knelt at the source of the Po to take a sample of spring water which he will transport along the river to the coast and Venice.
"This is a symbolic act," the bespectacled firebrand declared after holding up a specially-commissioned Venetian glass vial. "Water is the source of all things."

The journey along one of Europe's more polluted rivers prompted Ezio Mauro, editor of the Rome daily La Repubblica, to comment that Bossi needed the river "to unite the rebellious north-east with the old frustrated north-west".
He wrote that Bossi needed "something physical and mythological, natural and unstoppable that would be the same for all the various parts of northern Italy. It was the Po.
"Bossi must consecrate the river, turning it into the myth that makes Padania a nation...once again a nation will try to be born from a river, pretending it as sacred as the Nile."
The name "Padania" derives from the fertile Padana plain around the Po.
More symbols were evident as Bossi spoke to his green-shirted followers at Pian del Re on Friday evening.
A profusion of different flags fluttered in the wind.
There was the simple white cross on a red background and blue edging with the Northern league's medieval warrior raising aloft a broadsword in the centre of the flag.
The warrior harks back to the original Lega Lombarda (Lombard League) which was created in 1167 as an association of Lombard cities against the Emperor Barbarossa.
Elsewhere were red crosses, in both vertical and diagonal versions, against a white background.
The green six-rayed "Alpine Sun" on a white background fluttered from car sunroofs and along the road.
"The sun is truly the symbol of Padania, recognised above all factions and their individual objectives," declared a League pamphlet issued to reporters earlier in the day.

"There can be no better symbol than the sun to represent a country that has always kept its cultural unity despite centuries of political division and cultural domination, often imposed by force or treachery," it added.
Other flags depicted a gold sun on a red background -- the symbol of Occitania, a region in the south of France.
The golden lion of Venice was on yet another.

To add further variety, some cars parked on the mountain road had pink ribbons -- usually used to celebrate a birth and in this case that of Padania -- on radio aerials while displaying stickers with the Italian flag.
On Saturday and Sunday, the symbolism will extend to human chains along the banks of the Po and the protest burning of Italian state television licence forms.

Most Italians, however, have taken Bossi's drive for secession with a big pinch of salt. An opinion poll by Datamedia published on Friday showed only 7.6 percent were in favour of secession with 85.6 percent opposed.
